notes.title: Community Update: A New Direction
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

Thank you again for all your valuable feedback on the Norah's Song demo. Your insights have been incredibly helpful, and I truly appreciate the time and thought you put into trying it out.

After much consideration and deeply reviewing the comprehensive feedback, I've decided to shift to a completely new game idea. The demo served its purpose perfectly by highlighting the need to revisit some fundamental choices. Ultimately, as I looked at the final shape of Norah's Song and its storyline, I realized it wasn't aligning with the vision I had for a truly impactful experience, and frankly, I don't feel it's good enough for release.

This wasn't an easy decision, but the feedback you provided helped me see that an alternative concept carries more depth and offers greater potential for development. Rest assured, all the valuable input you shared will be carried forward and applied to this new project. My priority remains to build an even stronger, more polished experience that truly resonates with players.

This is all still a work in progress, and I'm excited about what's next. Thank you again for your detailed feedback.

notes.title: Development Update
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

Thank you again for all your valuable feedback on the Norah's Song demo. Your insights have been incredibly helpful.

I've decided to deactivate the demo for now. The comprehensive feedback highlighted the need to revisit some fundamental choices made during the game's development, which was exactly why I released the demo instead of developing blindly without community input. My priority is to ensure Norah's Song aligns as closely as possible with player interests and preferences while still retaining its unique identity. This step will help us build an even stronger, more polished experience for you.

This is all still a work in progress. Thank you again for your detailed feedback and for trying the demo!

notes.title: Demo Patch
notes.notes:
Hey everyone,

Thanks again for all the feedback on the Norah’s Song demo. I’ve just pushed an update that includes:

Fix for the clipping issue after the move to UE 5.6. It still happens in some edge cases with motion matching, which I’ll refine in a future update

Reduced head movement. A customization option for this and FOV is planned

Fixed the camera blur issue when toggling the flashlight or getting too close to walls

Fixed the camera going out of focus unexpectedly

To respond directly to a detailed comment that caught my attention:

Yes, the camera clipping is a real issue, especially around tight spaces like windows and lamps. I’m working on better collision handling to stop that from happening. The floaty camera and exaggerated wobble were toned down in this update, and more options are coming to let you adjust that to your preference.

The flashlight blur and strange focus behavior were caused by an unintended post-processing effect. That’s been fixed. As for the doors, you’re right. They lacked proper feedback, and input was getting stacked. I’ve started reworking the interaction system to feel more responsive and grounded.

This is all still a work in progress. I appreciate everyone’s patience and honesty. Every comment helps.

More updates soon.

Thank you copogu4, [dynamiclink href="https://steamcommunity.com/id/sonoket"][/dynamiclink], [dynamiclink href="https://steamcommunity.com/id/anothernewhuman"][/dynamiclink], [dynamiclink href="https://steamcommunity.com/id/caro12345/"][/dynamiclink] for your feedback and trying the demo!
